behavior: Forages for seeds and insects on the ground and among grass stems, often clinging to seed heads. Breeding males perform low, fluttering song flights; outside the nesting season, Bobolinks are social and often travel or feed in flocks.
field_marks: Compact songbird with a large, somewhat flat head and short neck.
Short, sharply pointed bill; pinkish in female and nonbreeding plumages, darker in breeding males.
Breeding male is black below and on the face, with a white back, shoulders, and rump plus a straw-colored nape.
Female and nonbreeding plumages are warm buff-brown with bold dark crown stripes, a dark eyeline, and streaked back and flanks.
Pointed wings and a short, rounded, multi-pointed tail.
Dark eyes and slender pinkish legs and feet.
habitat: Tall grasslands, uncut pastures, overgrown fields, meadows, and prairies; also marshes and agricultural fields during molt and migration.
